reading.name: Nigeria
reading.headline: Nigeria is in the Elevated tier (58/100, 31st riskiest of 203; 15th of 48 in Sub-Saharan Africa). Material risk on more than one front.
reading.ground: Expect periodic protests, policy surprises or economic stress. Contracts and plans can be upset by events outside your control, so they need contingencies and regular review.

drivers.label: Governance & Institutions
drivers.ground: Institutions you can't rely on: slow or biased courts, demands for bribes, rules that change without warning, weak protection of property and contracts.
drivers.felt_by: Businesses, investors and NGOs dealing with officials, permits, contracts or courts.
evidence: weak public services and policy delivery (33.6 WGI score, 0–100)

drivers.label: Political Stability & Violence
drivers.ground: Political violence, unrest and armed conflict: protests that shut roads and shops, attacks, curfews and, at the extreme, war.
drivers.felt_by: Everyone who is there (residents, staff and travellers) and anything with a fixed location.
evidence: a high perceived risk of political violence (35.1 WGI score, 0–100)

warnings.label: War-level violence (≥1,000 battle deaths in a year, UCDP threshold)
warnings.meaning: Armed conflict is killing people on a scale that counts as war or active conflict. Fighting can move fast, cut roads and supply lines, and spill into neighbouring areas.
warnings.response: Most governments advise against travel to affected areas; organisations limit presence to essential staff with security plans, and insurers treat the area as a war zone.

near: Inflation is 15.6%, approaching the 20% warning line.
The homicide rate is 16 per 100,000, approaching the warning line of 20.
direction: Over the longer run it has fallen from 63 in 2015 to 58 now.
events: General elections - presidency and National Assembly, 16 Jan 2027 (in 52 days, High significance)

business: Use the score to decide where to look closer: compare with peers (Peers tab) and read the drivers before deciding anything.
Raise due-diligence standards: vet partners and owners, enforce anti-bribery compliance, use international arbitration clauses, and consider political-risk insurance.
Plan for disruption: business-continuity and evacuation plans, security for staff and sites, and insurance that covers political violence.
Treat 'General elections - presidency and National Assembly' (16 Jan 2027) as a decision window: avoid locking in large, hard-to-reverse commitments just before it.
ngo: About 1.7% of the population is displaced: plan for shelter, protection, food and health needs through UN-led coordination (OCHA, UNHCR). The largest numbers abroad are in Niger, Cameroon and Canada.
Access and safety come first: negotiate access, apply humanitarian principles, and keep a security risk-management plan and duty of care for staff.
Expect bureaucratic hurdles and diversion risk: strengthen financial controls, partner vetting and accountability to affected people.
Movement and access may tighten around 'General elections - presidency and National Assembly' (16 Jan 2027): adjust field schedules and communications.
travel: Check your government's official travel advice for Nigeria before you go. It changes far faster than annual data.
There is active armed conflict: many governments advise against all or non-essential travel to the affected regions.
Higher violence and crime: avoid travelling at night, use trusted transport, keep a low profile and share your itinerary.
Stay away from demonstrations, especially around 'General elections - presidency and National Assembly' (16 Jan 2027). Protests can turn violent quickly.
research: Start with the drivers: Governance & Institutions and Political Stability & Violence carry the most risk. Explain why.
Put it in context: Nigeria ranks 15th of 48 in Sub-Saharan Africa and the Peers tab shows who is close.
Check whether changes are real: governance moves inside the WGI confidence intervals may be noise (Data tab, Governance).
Test the drivers: the What-if simulator shows which indicators would move the score most.
Write it up: the Assessment builder turns this into a structured brief with probabilities.

caveats: Scores are relative: they show where a country sits among the others and give no probability of any event.
The data look backwards: governance scores describe last year and conflict data lag by up to two years. Check current news and official travel advice.
This is general, educational guidance. It is not investment, legal or security advice.
